decisions.id: W40-3 tint: the class floor (row 634) relabeled CONVENTION
decisions.summary: judge_tint#one wet plot at least keeps its code and its claim is rewritten from a 0007 pointer to CONVENTION: 'when the draw leaves no low plot blue, the most basin-like one is tinted ... (0007 drawing records blue as a sample, not this floor)'
decisions.why: Round 1 allowed this row to stay open; taking it by relabel is a new decision and it is the exception path. impl-drift's DRIFTED note: '0007 ... describes blue as only the 45% draw on lowest-row plots on the drain; the promotion can tint a low plot up to LOW_ROWS off the drain'. The code is unchanged: the promotion's candidates are still p.get('low') (within LOW_ROWS row steps) or within a quarter plot of the collector, so it can still tint a plot 0007's own convention bullet does not ('A comb field gives each plot of its lowest row, the ones whose foot lies on the drain, a 45% chance of the tint'). FR-003: the claim alone is E0 only when a page not edited for the purpose already says what the code does, and 'any other rewrite of a DRIFTED row's claim is the exception path (FR-004)'; the new label concedes 0007 does not record the floor. A CONVENTION label is not checked against a page, so the drift is not fixed but taken out of the check's sight. Not impossible (the row's recorded fixes are both code changes), not implied by the GM's words ('I'm not sure there's any reason for our implementation to not match for anything'), and the purpose argument ('the map still shows the class it declares') is served equally by the ranker's first option. Fix: either take a recorded fix (restrict the promotion to a lowest-row plot on the drain - basin_rank already prefers one - after which a CONVENTION label for the existence of a floor the page is silent on is honest; or drop the promotion), or revert the relabel and leave row 634 open DRIFTED, as round 1 allowed.
